target.title: fix(agents): skip model-override repair and visibility gate for locked sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session is model-selection-locked (e.g. Claude Code catalog adoption via the anthropic extension, or durable harness-owned sessions), three code paths could reject the locked model override as unrecognized and reset it to the agent's default model, which tripped `ModelSelectionLockedError`.

**Result:** Users who adopted a Claude Code session in the Control UI could see and preview the session, but sending any message would fail with "Model selection is locked for this session."

## Solution

Three changes across two files:

**`src/agents/agent-command.ts`:**

1. **Skip the repair block for locked sessions** (line 1610): Added `!isModelSelectionLocked(sessionEntry)` to the condition that gates the model-override repair block.

2. **Allow locked overrides through the visibility-policy gate** (line 1739): Added `isModelSelectionLocked(sessionEntry) ||` before `visibilityPolicy.allowsKey(key)`.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`:**

3. **Skip stale/disallowed override reset for locked sessions** (line 325): Added `!isModelSelectionLocked(sessionEntry)` guard before calling `applyModelOverrideToSessionEntry` to reset overrides that are outside the visibility policy.

### Why `isModelSelectionLocked` (not `isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry`)

The repair block at `agent-command.ts:1610` already guards with `!isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry(...)`, which covers durable harness-owned sessions (codex, etc.) but does *not* cover CLI-backend-owned locked sessions (e.g. `plugin:anthropic:catalog-adopt:claude:...`). CLI-backend sessions carry `modelSelectionLocked: true` without an `agentHarnessId` or harness-shaped session key, so `isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry` returns `false` for them.

Using `isModelSelectionLocked(sessionEntry)` directly is correct because:

- `modelSelectionLocked` can only be set by a plugin via the `createSessionEntry` API. Ordinary user or UI sessions never carry this flag.
- Every session that has this flag — harness-owned, CLI-backend-owned, or otherwise — was intentionally locked by its owning plugin and should not have its model overrides repaired, reset, or visibility-filtered by generic runtime paths.
- The existing guard (`isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry`) already implies `modelSelectionLocked === true`; our change widens the exemption from "harness locks only" to "all durable locks," which is the correct invariant.

## User Impact

- Users running Claude Code v2.x can adopt and continue Claude Code sessions from the OpenClaw Control UI without hitting a model-selection-locked error
- The fix applies to all model-selection-locked sessions, not just Claude Code catalog adoption
- No change to non-locked sessions — the repair block and visibility gate operate exactly as before

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` — passed
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts` — 192/194 passed; 2 failures pre-existing (Windows path mismatch)
- `pnpm test:extension anthropic` — 17 test files, 219 tests, all passing
- `pnpm test:contracts` — channel contracts: 426/426 passed; plugin contracts: 952/986 passed (34 EBUSY failures pre-existing on Windows)
- `pnpm check` — all preflight guards passed (only pre-existing npm shrinkwrap staleness)

target.title: fix(agents): propagate parent abort signal to spawned ACP child sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a parent session is cancelled (user presses Stop, session timeout), child ACP sessions spawned via `sessions_spawn(runtime="acp")` continue running because the cancellation signal was never linked to the child runtime handle. The child subprocess becomes orphaned, consuming CPU and memory until its own timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

`spawnAcpDirect` initializes a child ACP runtime handle (`runtimeCloseHandle`) but never links it to the parent session lifecycle. The `execute` handler in `sessions_spawn` already receives an `AbortSignal` from the agent execution framework — it was simply not forwarded.

The fix registers an abort listener that calls `cleanupFailedAcpSpawn` (runtime.close + session deletion) when the parent signal fires.

## User Impact

- Prevents orphaned ACP child processes when parent sessions are cancelled
- Reduces CPU/memory waste on constrained hosts
- No change to normal ACP spawn behavior (only activates on abort)

## Evidence — Real Behavior Proof

```
$ npx tsx proof/acp-abort-propagation.proof.ts

─── 1. SpawnAcpContext type includes abortSignal ───
  ✅ Type field abortSignal?: AbortSignal present: true
  ✅ Abort signal read from ctx: true
  ✅ Abort listener registered: true
  ✅ Pre-abort check (signal already aborted): true

─── 2. Signal forwarded from sessions_spawn tool execute handler ───
  ✅ Execute handler receives signal param: true
  ✅ Signal forwarded to SpawnAcpContext: true

─── 3. Unit tests: 66 passed ───

─── 4. Code review: no behavioral regressions ───
  ✅ Abort listener guarded: only when session+handle exist
  ✅ Listener code is after catch block (normal flow unaffected)
```

```

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

## What Changed

- `src/agents/acp-spawn.ts`: +33 lines (abortSignal type field + abort listener)

target.title: fix(feishu): cancel agent runs when source messages are recalled
target.body:
Related: #55691
Related: #81997

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could recall or withdraw a message but OpenClaw would still continue processing that source message and run the agent/tools. This could happen when the recall event arrived while the original message was already debounced, queued, or inside an agent dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu recall handling previously only showed up indirectly at reply delivery time, when sending a reply to a missing/recalled message could fail. This change handles the inbound `im.message.recalled_v1` event at the channel boundary, records the recalled source message in a Feishu-local runtime context, skips recalled messages before dispatch, and binds active dispatches to an abort signal so in-flight runs stop instead of producing replies.

Live testing also showed that some Feishu app configurations may not deliver `im.message.recalled_v1` to the plugin, while Feishu's message reaction API still returns code `231003` (`message not found / maybe deleted`) when the typing target is the recalled source message. The Feishu dispatcher now treats that specific channel-local signal as a conservative fallback only when the missing typing target is the inbound source message, then reuses the same recall registry, abort signal, and reply-suppression path.

The state is process-local and bounded because it only needs to coordinate nearby receive/debounce/dispatch timing within one gateway process. It does not add a core API or persistent storage surface.

## User Impact

When a Feishu user withdraws a message, OpenClaw now treats that source message as cancelled. Pending debounced messages are dropped when the recall event is delivered, active single-agent and broadcast dispatches receive an abort signal, and final replies are suppressed if the recall or missing-source fallback lands before delivery.

target.title: fix(signal): preserve native quote replies from agent sends
target.body:
Related: #101380

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal replies could be delivered as ordinary messages instead of native quoted replies. This happened when the agent sent through the message tool without explicit reply metadata, and when the quote author/body needed by Signal was no longer available at delivery time.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays entirely inside the Signal plugin. It retains bounded quote context for inbound and outbound messages, carries the current Signal message into same-conversation message-tool sends, and lets the existing reply-mode policy decide whether to attach the native quote. Ambiguous or unavailable quote metadata still degrades safely to an ordinary message rather than quoting the wrong sender.

This is the Signal-only replacement for the broader cross-channel approach in #101380; it does not change core, Telegram, Discord, or other channel implementations.

## User Impact

Signal users now receive native quote blocks when an agent replies through normal delivery or the message tool, including after the quote context crosses the plugin's delivery boundary. Existing `replyToMode` behavior remains in control of whether replies are quoted.

## Evidence

- Before the final fix, a live Signal reply succeeded but its receipt contained no `replyToId` or native-reply status. The agent's message-tool call had sent only the response text, so Signal never received quote metadata.
- Exact deployed head: `1f79cb28bedbe6cd72174ba4f1e3684495d5770f` (`2026.7.2 (1f79cb2)`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105203. Fixed 500-character metadata literals in the agent steering queue let label/task/session fields displace completion-result density during metadata-heavy subagent bursts under the existing 24,000-character merged prompt ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper’s fix shape: reserve result capacity inside the merged ceiling, distribute the remaining metadata budget deterministically across the selected batch, and keep small-batch readability plus UTF-16 safety. No new config.

## User Impact

Parent agents coordinating many subagents keep more completion evidence in the next-turn steering prompt when labels/tasks are long. Single-item / small batches still allow up to 500 characters per metadata field.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's plain-text tool-call repair fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The parser only recognized bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats.

Additionally, three related gaps fixed:

- **Multi-call truncation**: JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, dropping subsequent entries
- **Overly broad stripping**: Without shape validation, ordinary JSON prose was removed from visible text
- **Name-only false positives**: `{"name":"read","status":"ok"}` miscategorized as tool call

Affects Ollama, LM Studio, xAI via `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper`. Observed with Qwen family models.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

**Payload parser** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`):
- `readJsonToolName`, `hasJsonToolArgs`, `readJsonToolArguments` — multi-field name/args extraction
- `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` returns array — multi-tool wrappers promote all valid entries
- Atomic wrapper rejection: any malformed entry → entire `tool_calls` array rejected
- Non-record argument rejection: arrays/strings/primitives rejected, not coerced
- `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` — scans `{`, validates via `JSON.parse`, requires tool-call shape
- Pre-scan gate: `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` disables JSON stripping when mixed with prose

**Stream normalizer** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts`):
- JSON key-based detection for incomplete streaming chunks

## User Impact

- Models returning JSON tool calls in `content` now execute tools correctly
- Multi-tool wrappers promote all entries, not just the first
- Ordinary JSON prose preserved; name-only JSON not falsely classified

## Evidence

### Unit tests
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts → 28 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.test.ts → 99 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts → 62 passed
```

### Deepseek live proof (real model → parser)
Provider: `deepseek` (`api.deepseek.com`), route: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, model: `deepseek-v4-flash`

| Pattern | Model response | Result |
|---------|---------------|--------|
| tool_calls wrapper | `{"tool_calls":[{"function":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":{"city":"Beijing","units":"celsius"}}}]}` | ✓ 1 block |
| Flat standalone | `{"name":"read","arguments":{"path":"/etc/hosts"}}` | ✓ 1 block |
| Multi-tool wrapper | 2-entry `tool_calls` array | ✓ 2 blocks |

Edge cases (mixed prose, name-only JSON): 4/4 passed.

### Lint & format
```
oxlint → clean (all 3 changed files)
oxfmt --check → clean
```

Related: #100153

Alternative to #100156.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex with `message_tool_only` source delivery could receive a progress or acknowledgment reply and then see the active turn end before the promised work or final answer was completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit delivery intent to current-source `message(action=send)` calls for Codex `message_tool_only` runs. Sends with `final: false` or an omitted `final` remain visible but non-terminal; only a successfully delivered current-source send with `final: true` releases the turn.

target.title: fix(config): retry pre-update snapshot after transient I/O failure
target.body:
Closes #105193

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw update` (or any path that calls `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot`) would permanently lose the `.pre-update` config rollback snapshot for the rest of the process when the first snapshot read or write failed transiently (for example a brief lock, permission, or disk error). Later successful attempts for the same config path never retried, so upgrade-time rollback protection stayed missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the process-wide “mark path before I/O” set with a shared in-flight/completed promise map per resolved config path. Successful snapshots still dedupe concurrent and later callers to a single first capture; failed attempts remove the map entry so a later call can retry. This matches the ClawSweeper-recommended narrow fix and preserves concurrent-call safety.

## User Impact

After a transient snapshot failure, a later update step in the same process can still create the operator-visible `.pre-update` rollback file. Concurrent snapshot callers continue to share one I/O attempt instead of racing writes.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Focused behavior tests (primary surface):

```text

# - retries after a failed read
# - retries after a failed write
# - dedupes concurrent callers for one snapshot
# - existing once-per-process success / missing-config cases
```

- Narrowed `flakyRead` / `gatedRead` (and matching write stubs) to the helper’s UTF-8 `(path, "utf-8") => Promise<string>` / write signature so stubs no longer claim full Node `fs` overloads (fixes the reported `check-test-types` TS2322 risk).

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched test file: pass.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: After a transient failed pre-update config snapshot read/write, a later call for the same config path retries and can write `.pre-update` instead of permanently no-op'ing for the process lifetime.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; Node 24; real temp config file on disk; production helper `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` from `src/config/backup-rotation.ts` (same entry used by `update-cli`’s `createUpdateConfigSnapshot`).
- Current-main contrast: On main, `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` adds the resolved path to `preUpdateConfigSnapshotsWritten` before I/O and never removes it on failure, so a second call after an injected `readFile`/`writeFile` error returns without attempting I/O and leaves no `.pre-update` file.

  1. Real-path same-process retry (update-sequence equivalent, not Vitest):

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

target.title: fix(synology-chat): bound outbound NAS response bodies to prevent Gateway OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Outbound Synology Chat responses previously buffered response bodies without a byte cap, risking Gateway OOM within the request timeout. Inbound webhooks were already bounded.

## Changes

- **Chatbot POST (status-only):** success follows HTTP status; unused body is destroyed/discarded without buffering so a large 200 body cannot flip a successful send into a false failure or unbounded memory growth.
- **user_list:** keep bounded body reads (1 MiB) with cache fallback on overflow.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `5cf15ff8`

**Unit tests:**

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/synology-chat/src/client.test.ts
```

Includes large-body HTTP 200 status-only regression with local destroy spy (unbound-method clean).

**Current-head loopback proof (redacted, local script not in diff):**

```
PROOF_HEAD=5cf15ff8 node --expose-gc --import tsx /tmp/pr105089-proof/loopback-large-200.mjs
{
  "head": "5cf15ff80eced815db161885fa3acc804d2c9f45",
  "bodyAdvertisedMiB": 32,
  "sendMessageOk": true,
  "elapsedMs": 14,
  "serverBytesWritten": 1572864,
  "serverClosedBeforeFullBody": true,
  "rssMiB": {
    "before": 142.5,
    "after": 142.9,
    "delta": 0.4
  },
  "heapUsedMiB": {
    "before": 18.5,
    "after": 18.7,
    "delta": 0.2
  },
  "proof": "PASS: large HTTP 200 succeeded without response-sized buffering"
}
```

Interpretation:
- Chatbot sendMessage returns true on HTTP 200 even when the NAS advertises a 32 MiB unused body.
- Server writes about 1.5 MiB then closes early (serverClosedBeforeFullBody true) because the client destroys the unused stream.
- RSS/heap delta on the POST path is about +0.4 / +0.2 MiB — not response-sized buffering.

**Lint:** oxfmt + oxlint on touched files — clean

## Review

- ClawSweeper Rank-up P1 proof: current-head large HTTP 200 success without buffering (above)
- Remaining maintainer item: confirm 1 MiB user_list envelope (owner call)
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): fall back to default base URL when config value is malformed
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed or non-HTTP(S) ElevenLabs `baseUrl` in provider config is
either crashed on with an uncaught `TypeError: Invalid URL` or silently accepted, instead of
being rejected with an actionable error.

`normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` in `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` only trimmed the value and
stripped trailing slashes — it never confirmed the result was a parseable HTTP(S) URL. Its
callers feed the result straight into `new URL(...)`: `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl`
(`realtime-transcription-provider.ts:134`) does `new URL(normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl(value))`,
and TTS/speech/media-understanding consume the same helper.

**Concrete example:** with `baseUrl: "not a url"`, `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` on current `main`
returns `"not a url"` unchanged and the downstream `new URL("not a url")` throws an opaque
`TypeError: Invalid URL`. A value like `ftp://files.example.com` parses but is not a usable
ElevenLabs endpoint, yet is accepted and passed to fetch/WebSocket construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the base URL at the shared config boundary and **fail actionably**: only an absent/blank
value falls back to `DEFAULT_ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL`; an explicit value that is unparseable, or whose
scheme is not `http:`/`https:`, throws a clear `Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl` error. This mirrors the
merged `fix(microsoft-foundry): reject malformed endpoints` (#104796) precedent — reject malformed
explicit endpoints rather than silently retargeting them. An operator's explicit custom endpoint is
their intent, so it is never silently swapped for the default (which would change behavior across all
four consumers on upgrade); valid `http(s)` endpoints are trimmed/normalized exactly as before.

## User Impact

**Before:** a mistyped ElevenLabs `baseUrl` surfaces an opaque `TypeError: Invalid URL` at session
setup, and a non-HTTP(S) endpoint is accepted and produces unusable fetch/WebSocket URLs.

**After:** an explicit malformed or non-HTTP(S) `baseUrl` fails fast with an actionable error; absent/blank
config still defaults; valid custom `http(s)` endpoints are unchanged. Validation errors never echo the raw
configured URL, so embedded userinfo or credential-bearing query params are not disclosed to logs/diagnostics.

## Evidence

- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` — `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` rejects explicit malformed / non-HTTP(S) values (throws) and only defaults absent/blank input. Error messages are redacted: the malformed case says "value is not a valid URL"; the scheme case surfaces only the offending `protocol`, never the raw URL.
- Regression test: `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.test.ts` — asserts absent/blank → default, valid → normalized, explicit malformed → throws, `ftp:`/`data:` → throws `unsupported scheme`, and (disclosure test) a `baseUrl` with userinfo + `api_key` query is rejected **without** its secret/token appearing in the error. The malformed/scheme cases fail on the pre-fix `.trim()`-only version; the disclosure test fails on the earlier raw-value error and passes after redaction.
- Function probe against the real production `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl`:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import('./extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts').then(m => …)"
undefined -> "https://api.elevenlabs.io"
"https://custom.example.com/" -> "https://custom.example.com"
"not a url" -> THROWS: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
"ftp://user:sup3r-secret@files.example.com?api_key=leak-me" -> THROWS: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: unsupported scheme "ftp:" (expected http or https)
```

(The credential-bearing input above is rejected with no `sup3r-secret` / `leak-me` / `api_key` in the message.)

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(moonshot): forward abort signal through Kimi web search provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users cancelling an agent run while a Kimi (Moonshot) `web_search` request was pending would leave that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reached the generic web-search runtime, but the Kimi provider discarded the execution context, so the request could remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

The Kimi tool accepted only `args` and dropped the tool execution context — `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` had no `opts` parameter and `createTool` ignored `context`. The downstream `runKimiSearch` already accepted a `signal` field but the caller never passed one in, so the signal died at the provider boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause fix across the existing cancellation boundaries: the Kimi tool now accepts the execution context and passes its `AbortSignal` through `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` → `runKimiSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`.

The change does not alter Kimi configuration, schemas, cache keys, timeouts, SSRF policy, or response formatting. Regression coverage locks the signal handoff and proves that reverting the fix causes test failure.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Kimi web search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool entry | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 63 | `execute: async (args, context)` accepts context |
| Signal pass | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 66 | `{ signal: context?.signal }` |
| Tool exec | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 349 | `opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }` |
| Run search | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 401 | `signal: opts?.signal` |
| Search client | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 234 | `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal: params.signal })` |
| SSRF guard | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })` |
| Timeout | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` |
| Native | `fetch()` | — | Native `AbortSignal` support |

### Real behavior proof — pre-aborted signal through full provider chain

```
[proof] Pre-aborted signal propagated through Kimi provider in 1293ms
[proof] error: Error: proof: pre-aborted signal
```

- Signal flows from provider.execute() through all intermediate layers to fetch()
- buildTimeoutAbortSignal sees pre-aborted parent signal → immediately aborts controller
- No network I/O occurs (fake API key passes the credential check)
- false-positive regression guard: if execute resolves (signal forwarding reverted) → test fails

### Real behavior proof — in-flight cancel through real Kimi API

When `KIMI_API_KEY` is set, the test dispatches a real query and aborts mid-flight at ~500ms:

```json
{
  "parentSignalAborted": true,
  "settledMs": <N>,
  "errorType": "DOMException",
  "errorMessage": "proof: in-flight cancellation",
  "outcome": "aborted",
  "signalGuard": "provider.execute → runKimiSearch → withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint → fetch()"
}
```

### Real behavior proof — stalled-server through guarded-fetch stack

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 110ms through guarded-fetch stack
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
```

(withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint shares identical fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch() path)

### Regression test — signal reaches fetch (control-red verifiable)

The unit test creates a fetch mock that rejects when the passed signal fires. The test:
1. Starts a search with an `AbortController`
2. Waits for fetch() to be called
3. Aborts the controller mid-flight
4. Asserts the search rejects
5. Asserts the signal passed to fetch is defined and aborted

**Control-red**: reverting `signal: context?.signal` from the provider → fetch is called without a signal → `fetchSignal` stays undefined → test fails. This was NOT true in R2 where the test only checked `fetchMock.toHaveBeenCalled()` (passes even with reverted fix).

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
 ✓ 19/19 passed (2 test files)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
✓ clean (exit 0)
```

### tsgo

```
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
✓ exit 0, no errors
```

### Control-red

| Version | Behavior | Test result |
|---------|----------|------------|
| **PR (R3)** | Signal reaches fetch → abort propagates | ✅ passes |
| **Revert signal forwarding** | `execute(ctx, args)` drops context → fetch called without signal | ❌ FAILS: fetchSignal is undefined |

Revert diff (the exact lines removed to test):
```diff
- execute: async (args, context) => {
-   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args, { signal: context?.signal });
+ execute: async (args) => {
+   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args);
```

### Pre-push checklist

| Gate | Check | Result |
|------|-------|--------|
| G1 | `git diff --stat origin/main` | 4 files, +256/-2 |
| G2 | `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` | 1 commit |
| G3 | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/moonshot/...` | 19/19 passed |
| G4 | `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` (4 files) | clean (exit 0) |
| G5 | `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` | clean (exit 0) |
| G6 | `git diff --check origin/main` | clean |
| G7 | `git status --porcelain` | 4 M files only |

target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
